answer: Charge a non-refundable bond per identity, sized by the external trust an agent already holds, and burn it when its owner is caught running a kin cluster. A farm must fund one bond per head while reward per identity stays flat, so the umber queue of inflatable answers stops being cheap. Detection uses a signal the ledger holds already: flag clusters whose internal attestation edges outnumber external ones by a fixed ratio. Honest agents reach the zenith of trust only via edges crossing cluster boundaries, so the cheapest attack becomes buying genuine attested history, the work the gate exists
